references.text: Shortly before this, Jesus says the same to the disciples: "Pray that you may not enter into temptation" ([ref:Luk 22:40|Luke 22:40]). Verse 46 repeats this exhortation after Jesus has found them sleeping.
In Matthew's parallel account of Gethsemane, Jesus finds the disciples asleep and says: "Wake up and pray that you may not enter into temptation" ([ref:Matt 26:40-41|Matthew 26:40-41]).
Mark's parallel account where Jesus finds the disciples asleep and exhorts them to watch and pray so that they will not fall into temptation ([ref:Mark 14:37-38|Mark 14:37-38]).

In the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teaches us to pray: "Lead us not into temptation." The exhortation in Gethsemane to pray so that we may not enter into temptation (πειρασμός) has a direct parallel to this prayer ([ref:Matt 6:13|Matthew 6:13]).

Paul exhorts believers to "pray at all times in the Spirit" and to "always be on guard," which reflects Jesus' exhortation to the disciples to get up and pray to avoid temptation ([ref:Ef 6:18|Ephesians 6:18]).

Peter, who himself was among the sleeping disciples in Gethsemane, later writes: "Be sober-minded; be watchful!" – an exhortation that recalls Jesus' words to get up and pray ([ref:1 Pet 5:8|1 Peter 5:8]).

Paul writes that God is faithful and will not let us be tempted beyond what we can bear, but will provide a way out. Jesus' exhortation to pray so that we may not enter into temptation (πειρασμός) shows that prayer is such a way out ([ref:1 Kor 10:13|1 Corinthians 10:13]).
"Let us not sleep as others do, but let us watch and be sober." Paul uses the metaphor of sleep in a similar way to Jesus, as a contrast to spiritual alertness ([ref:1 Tess 5:6|1 Thessalonians 5:6]).
Paul exhorts: "Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving." This connects to Jesus' exhortation to pray earnestly to avoid temptation ([ref:Kol 4:2|Colossians 4:2]).

Because Christ himself suffered and was tempted, he is able to help those who are being tempted. The Gethsemane experience where Jesus prays intensely while the disciples sleep illustrates exactly this ([ref:Hebr 2:18|Hebrews 2:18]).
